security_audit.summary: All 115 static findings are false positives after contextual review. They represent Markdown syntax, chemistry notation, expected output writes, dictionary keys, or normal error messages. A separate high-severity issue remains because SKILL.md demonstrates unsafe pickle deserialization without a trust warning.

remediation.suggestion: Warn users never to load untrusted pickle files, and recommend SDF or SMILES for data exchange.

content.value_statement: Advanced molecular workflows require careful control over parsing, descriptors, fingerprints, and structure queries. This skill provides focused RDKit guidance, references, and reusable scripts.
actual_capabilities: Parse SMILES, SDF, MOL, InChI, and molecule blocks with validation guidance.
Calculate molecular weight, LogP, TPSA, hydrogen-bond counts, QED, and other descriptors.
Generate molecular fingerprints and compare structures with Tanimoto, Dice, or cosine similarity.
Filter molecule collections with custom SMARTS patterns and predefined structural libraries.
Generate 2D depictions, 3D conformers, alignments, and highlighted substructure images.
Guide reaction SMARTS, molecular modification, standardization, and scaffold analysis.
limitations: Python and RDKit must be installed separately before running the examples or scripts.
The included scripts support common molecular formats but do not cover every RDKit data source.
Descriptor values and structure matches require scientific review for each research context.
3D conformers and force-field results depend on molecular preparation, parameters, and random seeds.

use_cases.title: Screen Compound Libraries
use_cases.description: Calculate properties, apply structural filters, and rank compounds by fingerprint similarity.

use_cases.title: Prepare Molecular Features
use_cases.description: Create validated descriptors and fingerprints for modeling, clustering, or exploratory analysis.

use_cases.title: Build Reproducible Structure Workflows
use_cases.description: Design parsing, sanitization, conformer generation, reaction, and visualization workflows with explicit parameters.

prompt_templates.title: Calculate Basic Properties
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze the SMILES CCO. Report molecular weight, LogP, TPSA, hydrogen-bond donors, hydrogen-bond acceptors, and Lipinski status.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Descriptor Export
prompt_templates.prompt: Review molecules.smi and prepare a command to calculate descriptors into properties.csv. Explain how invalid molecules are handled.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Similarity Search
prompt_templates.prompt: Search database.sdf for compounds similar to c1ccccc1 using Morgan fingerprints and a 0.70 Tanimoto threshold. Summarize the top hits.

prompt_templates.title: Design an Advanced Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an RDKit workflow that filters PAINS, computes custom descriptors, clusters Morgan fingerprints, generates conformers, and records validation failures.

output_examples.input: Calculate drug-likeness properties for the SMILES CCO.
output: Lipinski result: passes the standard thresholds

output_examples.input: Filter a molecule file to retain benzene-containing structures.
output: Use the benzene SMARTS pattern c1ccccc1.
Write passing structures to the requested SDF or SMILES output.

output_examples.input: Plan a Morgan fingerprint similarity screen.
output: Use a documented radius and fingerprint size.
Calculate Tanimoto similarity against the query fingerprint.
Sort matches from highest to lowest score and apply the selected threshold.

best_practices: Check every parsed molecule for None before calculating properties or fingerprints.
Validate SMARTS patterns and document fingerprint parameters, thresholds, and random seeds.
Use exchange formats such as SDF or SMILES for untrusted data instead of pickle files.
anti_patterns: Do not process invalid molecules without checking parser results.
Do not compare similarity scores generated with different fingerprint settings.
Do not load pickle files from untrusted or unknown sources.

faq.question: Does this skill install RDKit?
faq.answer: No. Install RDKit in the active Python environment before running examples or scripts.

faq.question: Which molecular formats are supported?
faq.answer: The guidance covers SMILES, SDF, MOL, InChI, molecule blocks, and common compressed workflows.

faq.question: Can it calculate drug-likeness properties?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers molecular weight, LogP, TPSA, hydrogen-bond counts, QED, and Lipinski checks.

faq.question: Can it search large molecule collections?
faq.answer: Yes. The references include streaming suppliers, bulk similarity methods, and a fingerprint search script.

faq.question: When should I use Datamol instead?
faq.answer: Use Datamol for simpler standard workflows. Use this RDKit skill when you need detailed control or specialized algorithms.

faq.question: Are pickle molecule files safe to share?
faq.answer: Treat pickle files as executable content. Load them only from trusted sources, and prefer SDF or SMILES for exchange.
